label: two steps after a 3 that is followed by 0/3, in sequences starting with 3/k/p/a
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.01% of steps). Fires almost entirely in the original phase and at the delimiter (89% + 9% of mass), most often at early positions (t=2-4), never at t=0/1, and almost never in the copy phase. Its strongest cue is that the input two steps back was the digit 3 (prev2_tok==3 covers 78% of mass, 30x lift), more so when the intervening token is 0 or 3 (e.g. prefixes 3 0 _, 3 3 _, k 3 3 _), and the sequence starts with 3, k, p or a (first_tok 3 alone covers 48% of mass, k 32%). Sequences with more digits light it up more often. Magnitude is small and uniform (median 0.12, max 0.20). The top activations are in k/p-initial digit-heavy sequences such as k 3 y 3 [y] or p 3 3 3 [y]. Even with all these conditions precision stays low (~0.2): most steps with 3 two back do not fire, so it depends on more of the prefix than these variables capture. A narrower version (3 at t=0, then 0 or 3) reaches dev F1 0.39 but loses recall.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=k (+5.73), t=2 & prev_tok=0 (+5.60), prev2_tok=3 (+4.22), orig0=p (+3.50), prev_tok=3 (+3.39), t=2 & prev_tok=i (+3.31). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.01), phase=2 (-4.19), prev2_tok=k (-2.31), in_tok=g (-2.07).
